In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best approach to early recurrence in favorable stage I and II breast cancer is to use a multimodality treatment.

the results of the present study indicate that the use of the 21-gene recurrence score assay (RS) in the decision making for adjuvant chemotherapy in patients with stage I-II, ER-positive, HER2-negative, node-negative breast cancer is not recommended.

there are no clear indications for the use of adjuvant chemotherapy for stage II breast cancer patients with a favorable prognosis, i.e. with no evidence of lymph node metastases, and with a tumor of 2 cm or less in diameter.

we have shown that the use of a 2D/3D hybrid approach to the analysis of 2D and 3D breast cancer data can be useful in the analysis of breast cancer data.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a single dose of radiation therapy is safe and effective in the treatment of early-stage breast cancer.
the current approach of using a 2-3 year adjuvant endocrine therapy is not optimal for the majority of women with hormone receptor positive, HER2-negative breast cancer.
